text:
Ah, yes. The toothbrush. A simple, bristled stick that requires zero cardiovascular effort and yields immediate, tangible results. It is the true pinnacle of human innovation, far surpassing the fitness industry’s latest miracle cure: the "Shake-and-Bake" dumbbell.

Why, indeed, would anyone waste precious hours sweating, grunting, and feeling actual physical discomfort when they could simply hold a piece of plastic and mimic the motion of stirring a pot of soup? The logic is impeccable. If I can achieve the physique of a Greek statue by flicking my wrist for ten minutes while watching a sitcom, then clearly, the concept of "muscle tension" is just a myth invented by gyms to sell overpriced water bottles.

It is truly the epitome of effortlessness. Who needs biology, physics, or consistency when you have a plastic weight that weighs less than a smartphone? I am currently on day three of my routine, and I am already seeing results. My arms are tired from the sheer mental exhaustion of pretending this is a workout. I am, in fact, sculpting my body into a Greek statue of confusion. But hey, at least I’m not sweating. And in the modern world, isn’t that the only metric that truly matters?
